h1.span: Before You Begin: Scope and Applicability

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

div.p: This guide is for beginner-to-intermediate desktop FDM users who can clean the build plate, run a first-layer test, and adjust basic slicer settings such as build plate temperature or brim settings.
Use the table below to confirm whether this troubleshooting path matches your situation.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

tr.td: Edge or corner lifting during printing
Full detachment in the first layers
Temperature error, failed heating, or unstable hardware temperature
Manufacturer guidance conflicts with this guide

div.p: If more than one condition applies, address any hardware, temperature-control, or build plate issue before changing slicer settings. Follow manufacturer documentation when it provides product-specific instructions.

h1.span: Quick checklist for edge lifting troubleshooting

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

div.p: Start with this checklist before changing advanced slicer settings.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

tr.td: Surface contamination is a common first-layer issue.
Poor first-layer contact often causes early lifting.
Recheck bed leveling or first-layer calibration.
Weak adhesion may appear after printing starts.
Confirm the PLA profile and build plate temperature.
Uneven cooling can make one side lift more easily.
Some shapes create more shrinkage stress.
Test bottom surface or infill pattern changes only after the basic checks.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

tr.td: Adhesion is inconsistent across the build plate
Small prints lift even when settings appear normal
One corner lifts more than the others
One side of the model sticks better than the other
Large flat models fail after a normal start
Build plate temperature, edge adhesion, and part geometry
Build plate temperature (on page ), Edge adhesion (on page ), then Part geometry (on page )
The same model sometimes succeeds and sometimes fails
Large flat models still fail after all basic checks
Secondary slicer settings such as bottom surface pattern or infill pattern

div.p: If your situation matches more than one row, start from the earliest step in the recommended troubleshooting order.

h1.span: Fix edge lifting and minor warping in PLA prints

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

div.p: If a PLA print starts normally but the lower edges or corners lift from the build plate during printing, follow these steps to diagnose and resolve the issue.
Note: Change only one setting or environmental factor at a time. After each change, test under the same conditions before changing another factor.

The nozzle and heated build plate can remain hot before, during, and after printing. Let the printer cool down, or follow the manufacturer's safety guidance before cleaning the build plate or making manual adjustments.

h2.span: Build plate surface is dirty or poorly prepared

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping
Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

div.p: Dust, oil, fingerprints, or leftover residue on the build plate can reduce first-layer adhesion.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Small prints lift even when settings appear normal.
Adhesion is inconsistent across the build plate.
A print starts normally but loses contact later.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Clean the build plate according to the manufacturer's care guidance.
Do not touch the print area after cleaning.

li.p: Confirm that the selected build surface profile, or the printer or slicer setting for the installed plate type, matches the installed build surface.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Restart the same print or run the same first-layer test under the same conditions.
If the first layer stays attached across the print area, stop here and keep the build plate preparation method.
If adhesion is still inconsistent, continue to first-layer height or bed leveling checks.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Cleaning methods vary by build surface.

h2.span: First-layer height or bed leveling is incorrect

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping
Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

div.p: If the nozzle is too close to the build plate or too far from it, the first layer may not form stable contact.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Extruded lines look too round and loose.
Extruded lines look too thin and overly squashed.
One side of the model sticks better than the other.
Edge lifting starts from one area of the build plate.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Recheck bed leveling or first-layer calibration.
Use a simple first-layer test print if one is available.
Adjust the nozzle-to-build-plate distance in small increments. On printers that provide a Z-offset or other micron-based height adjustment, about 0.02 mm can be used as a cautious starting point.
After each adjustment, repeat the same first-layer test before starting another full print.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Repeat the same first-layer test after each adjustment.

li.p: If the first-layer lines show stable contact across the build plate, stop here and keep the current calibration.

ul.li: If one side still sticks better than the other, recheck bed leveling before changing slicer settings.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: A first-layer calibration print or first-layer test print is usually a more reliable way to confirm contact.

span.span: First-layer line shape changes when the nozzle is too high, correctly set, or too low.

img.alt: Three side-by-side examples of first-layer extrusion showing a nozzle position that is too high, correct, and too low.
img.css:oxy-alt-text: Three side-by-side examples of first-layer extrusion showing a nozzle position that is too high, correct, and too low.

h2.span: Build plate temperature is too low or unstable

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping
Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

div.p: If the build plate is too cool, the first layer may not bond strongly enough to resist shrinkage stress at the edges. If the build plate temperature is unstable, adhesion may also become less consistent during printing.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: The print starts normally but corners lift later.
Larger flat models fail more easily than smaller ones.
Prints fail more often in cooler conditions.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: For PLA on a heated bed, 50–60°C is a common reference range. If the manufacturer recommends a different value, follow that value.

li.p: If corners lift after the print starts and the current value is near the lower end of the recommended range, test a slightly higher build plate temperature under the same conditions.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Restart the same print after changing only the build plate temperature.
If the lower edges stay attached through the early layers, stop here and keep the tested temperature.
If corners still lift, return to the previous temperature before testing another factor.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: A higher build plate temperature is not a universal fix.
This factor often interacts with first-layer contact, part size, and room conditions.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping
Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

div.p: The base of the model may not have enough contact area to resist upward pulling force.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Corners lift first even when the center still holds.
Narrow-base parts detach more easily.
Tall parts with a small footprint become unstable.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Add a brim to increase contact area around the model.
Start with the slicer’s default brim setting or a narrow brim, and increase the width one step at a time only if edge lifting continues.
Use a brim before moving to more advanced slicer changes.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Restart the same print with the brim enabled.
If the corners and narrow contact areas stay attached, stop here and keep the brim setting.
If lifting continues, increase the brim width one step at a time.
If a wider brim does not improve the result, check airflow, room conditions, or part geometry instead.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: A brim may leave extra material around the model base that must be removed after printing.

span.span: A brim increases contact area around the model base and helps resist edge lifting.

img.alt: Two views of a model on a build plate, one printed without a brim and one with a brim extending around the base.
img.css:oxy-alt-text: Two views of a model on a build plate, one printed without a brim and one with a brim extending around the base.

h2.span: Airflow or room conditions cause uneven cooling

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping
Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

div.p: Drafts or unstable room temperature can cool one side of the print faster than the other. Uneven cooling can increase shrinkage stress along one edge or corner.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: One corner lifts more than the others.
The same model sometimes succeeds and sometimes fails.
Problems occur more often near windows, fans, or air vents.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Reduce direct airflow around the printer.
Avoid sudden airflow or temperature changes during printing.
Avoid placing the printer near open windows, fans, air vents, or other strong moving air sources.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Restart the same print after reducing direct airflow around the printer.
If the same corner or side no longer lifts under similar conditions, stop here and keep the more stable airflow setup.
If the issue appears only at certain times or locations, review nearby airflow sources again.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: For PLA printing, a full enclosure is not required in many normal cases.
Small changes in airflow can still affect build plate adhesion, especially on larger flat parts.
More stable room conditions may help reduce repeated edge lifting.

h2.span: Part geometry or orientation increases shrinkage stress

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping
Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

div.p: Large flat bases, long straight edges, and sharp corners can concentrate shrinkage stress during cooling.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Long rectangular parts lift at both ends.
Sharp corners lift more easily than rounded ones.
Lifting begins along long exposed edges on otherwise well-adhered parts.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Reconsider the print orientation if possible.
Avoid placing long straight edges directly along the build plate when another orientation is possible.
Reduce long exposed edge length when the model allows it.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Test the same model in the revised orientation when possible.
If edge lifting is reduced under the same printing conditions, stop here and use the revised orientation for this model.
If orientation changes do not reduce lifting, return to the basic adhesion checks or consider model-specific design changes.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Some shapes create more stress even when first-layer calibration and build plate adhesion are acceptable.

h2.span: Use secondary slicer adjustments only after the basic checks

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

div.p: Use the following slicer-level adjustments only after checking build plate condition, first-layer contact, build plate temperature, edge adhesion, airflow, and part geometry.
These adjustments do not replace model-specific design changes when the model shape itself causes repeated lifting.

h3.span: Bottom surface pattern may affect stress distribution

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping
Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

div.p: On some large flat models, the bottom surface pattern may influence how cooling stress becomes visible across the base.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Large flat models continue to show edge lifting after all basic checks.
Edge lifting appears in a similar location each time when the same slicer profile is used.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Test one alternative bottom surface pattern, such as Concentric or Zigzag, on the same model.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Test only one alternative bottom surface pattern on the same model.
If edge lifting is reduced under the same printing conditions, stop here and keep the tested bottom surface pattern for this model.
If the result does not improve, return to the previous pattern before testing another slicer setting.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: On some flat parts, line-based paths may create longer continuous stress paths across the base.
No bottom surface pattern works best for every model.

h3.span: Infill pattern may affect internal stress behavior

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping
Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

div.p: The infill pattern may affect how cooling stress builds inside the part after the base is already attached.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Minor warping remains after first-layer correction and brim use.
The base adheres well at first, but warping develops as the print grows taller.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Test an alternative infill pattern on the same model.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Test only one alternative infill pattern on the same model.
If minor warping is reduced after the base has already adhered, stop here and keep the tested infill pattern for this model.
If the result does not improve, return to the previous infill pattern before testing another slicer setting.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

ul.li: Some infill patterns create longer crossing paths or a different material distribution inside the part.
Results vary by model.

span.span: Internal patterns can change how stress paths are distributed inside a part.

img.alt: A simplified comparison of path layouts on a flat printed part, showing that different bottom and internal path strategies can distribute stress in different ways.
img.css:oxy-alt-text: A simplified comparison of path layouts on a flat printed part, showing that different bottom and internal path strategies can distribute stress in different ways.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

div.p: If edge lifting continues after the basic checks, stop changing slicer settings and narrow down the next likely cause.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

tr.td: No extrusion or failed startup appears
The build plate cannot hold the target temperature
The build plate is damaged, loose, or heavily worn
The same PLA spool fails on simple models
Try a known good PLA spool
Check airflow and clean the build plate again
Large flat models still fail after the basic checks
Test one secondary slicer adjustment at a time
The issue starts after a slicer profile change
Compare with a known good profile

div.p: Stop here if the issue appears to be hardware-related. Follow printer-specific or slicer-specific documentation before making more changes.

h1.span: Why PLA prints develop edge lifting and minor warping

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping
Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

div.p: PLA cools and shrinks slightly as each layer is deposited. That shrinkage creates an upward pulling force on the lower edges of the part.
The build plate must hold the part down while this happens. When the shrinkage force becomes stronger than build plate adhesion, the edges begin to lift.

span.span: Edge lifting begins when cooling shrinkage overcomes build plate adhesion at the edge.

img.alt: A simple diagram of a printed part on a build plate, with arrows showing upward pulling force from cooling shrinkage and downward holding force from build plate adhesion.
img.css:oxy-alt-text: A simple diagram of a printed part on a build plate, with arrows showing upward pulling force from cooling shrinkage and downward holding force from build plate adhesion.

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

div.p: Corners often lift first because they have less surrounding material and more exposure to open-air cooling. Once a corner lifts, the nearby edge often follows.

h2.span: Why large flat parts warp more easily

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

div.p: Large flat parts create more total shrinkage stress as PLA cools.
Long straight edges can also accumulate stress in one direction. This can make the lower perimeter more likely to pull away from the build plate.
For that reason, parts that look simple because they have a large flat base may actually be harder to keep fully attached during printing.

h2.span: Why the first layers matter most

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

div.p: The first layers determine how well the rest of the part stays anchored to the build plate.
If first-layer contact is weak, later shrinkage forces become more visible. As the print grows taller, the lower edges may be pulled upward more easily.
For that reason, edge lifting and minor warping often begin as an early first-layer problem, even when the print continues for some time afterward.

h1.span: Key terms for PLA edge lifting troubleshooting

div.div: Xinyue Chen
Troubleshooting Edge Lifting and Minor Warping

tr.td: The first printed layer placed directly onto the build plate. Its quality affects how well the rest of the part stays attached during printing.
The process of checking and adjusting first-layer contact so that the printed lines bond correctly to the build plate.
The ability of a printed part to stay attached to the build plate while it is being printed.
A thin ring of extra printed material added around the base of a part to increase contact area.
A printer setting that adjusts the nozzle height relative to the build plate. It is often used to fine-tune first-layer contact.
The slicer or printer setting that matches the installed build surface or plate type.
The path strategy used for the solid bottom layers where the print meets the build plate.
The path pattern used to print the internal support structure inside a part.

div.p: Note: Bottom surface pattern affects the solid lower surface. Infill pattern affects the internal structure.
